title: Uncertainty-Aware Execution: Conformal Prediction vs. Reinforcement Learning for Optimal Trade Execution
description:
Reference implementation and reproducibility package for the paper Uncertainty-Aware AI: Conformal Prediction versus Reinforcement Learning for Optimal Trade Execution (Irshad & Biswas, Statistics, Optimization & Information Computing, 16(2), 1334–1349, 2026; DOI 10.19139/soic-2310-5070-4159).

The package contains a self-contained VWAP-execution simulator with stochastic volatility and latent AR(1) return momentum, classical execution schedules (Immediate, TWAP, Almgren–Chriss, VWAP-tracking), a multi-seed PPO agent, and forecast-driven policies built on a normalised split-conformal predictor of next-interval returns. The central contribution is the use of the conformal interval width as an explicit gate on execution decisions: the policy acts on the return forecast only when its magnitude exceeds kappa times the conformal half-width, and otherwise falls back to VWAP tracking. Sweeping kappa traces a monotone cost–risk frontier that reduces the variance of execution cost at almost no cost in the mean, and does so more reproducibly than the reinforcement-learning agent.

All scripts regenerate every table and figure from seed. Simulator-based research; no live-trading claims.
